findings.title: Authorized-user check is skipped entirely when no Integration row exists
findings.body: When no Integration matches the installation_id, the code hits `except Integration.DoesNotExist: return pipeline.next_step()` and never compares `github_authenticated_user` against anyone. The sender comparison (lines 501-505) runs only when a row already exists, and that row is normally written by the installation webhook. For a fresh install where the webhook has not yet been processed, any request carrying that installation_id passes without the user check. The PR describes this check as the protection against a mismatched installer, so this is fail-open in exactly the first-install case. Consider failing closed, or obtaining the installer identity from the GitHub API instead of relying on a DB row that may not exist yet.

findings.title: KeyError on integration.metadata['sender'] for integrations without sender metadata
findings.body: `integration.metadata['sender']['login']` assumes the key exists. Integrations created by the pipeline without a sender in state do not have it: test_basic_flow asserts the exact metadata dict, which has no 'sender' key. If such a row exists without an OrganizationIntegration (the only branch that reaches this line), reinstalling the app raises KeyError and returns a 500 instead of the failure page. Use a safe lookup such as `.get('sender', {}).get('login')` and treat a missing value as a mismatch.

findings.title: Installer lookup is not scoped to the GitHub provider
findings.body: `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id, status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE)` does not filter by `provider=GitHubIntegrationProvider.key`. Integration uniqueness is per (provider, external_id), so a non-GitHub integration sharing the same external_id can be returned, and its metadata then drives the GitHub authorization decision. If several rows match, `get` raises MultipleObjectsReturned, which is uncaught and produces a 500. The earlier lookup at line 478 has the same omission, but this new lookup is the one feeding the authorization check.

findings.title: Error strings are no longer extracted for translation
findings.body: `error()` wraps the non-literal `error_short` in `_()` at call time, and the callers pass plain English strings (for example 'Github installed on another Sentry organization.' and 'GitHub installation pending deletion.'). Message extraction only picks up literal arguments to `_()`, so these strings are no longer in the message catalogs and will never be translated. The previous code had literal `_(...)` calls at these sites, so this is a regression. Mark the strings with `_()` at the call sites instead.

findings.title: Network failure during token exchange escapes the error handling
findings.body: `safe_urlopen` at line 423 is outside the try block that guards response parsing, and `get_user_info` at line 434 is not guarded either. A connection error or timeout talking to github.com raises an unhandled exception, so the user gets a 500 instead of the rendered failure page. Every other failure in this view returns `error(...)`, so these calls should be guarded too.

findings.title: installation_id is persisted to pipeline state before the state parameter is verified
findings.body: `pipeline.bind_state('installation_id', installation_id)` runs before the `state` check at lines 412-413. A request with a wrong or forged state still overwrites the stored installation_id and then gets the error page. PipelineAdvancer sets `csrf_protect = False`, so a cross-site request can mutate an in-progress pipeline. Bind the value only after the state has been validated.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer tests installation-not-found
findings.body: The test now sends a wrong `state` and asserts the generic 'Invalid installation request.' page. The 404 mock on the installation endpoint is never reached, and the 'The GitHub installation could not be found.' IntegrationError path in build_integration is no longer exercised by any test. The test name no longer matches what it asserts. Restore a test that drives the pipeline through build_integration with a 404, or rename this test and add a separate case.

findings.title: No test covers successful verification or the new token and user-info failure branches
findings.body: test_github_user_mismatch covers only the negative case. Nothing verifies that the pipeline completes when the webhook sender matches the authenticated login (octocat). The new failure branches in OAuthLoginView (missing access_token, missing login from get_user_info, and state mismatch aside from the one in test_installation_not_found) are also untested. These are the security-relevant paths this PR adds, so the positive case and each failure branch should have a test.
